To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the production of K+ is enhanced in alpha induced reactions compared to deuteron induced reactions.
the K + yield in the midrapidity region of d + A collisions is enhanced by a factor of 2 with respect to the π + yield, while the enhancement factor for the K + yield is 4 in the α + A collisions.
the K + yield in d + Au collisions is about 2.5 times higher than in p + Au collisions, and the K + yield is about 4 times higher in α + Au collisions than in d + Au reactions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the production of subthreshold particles in nuclear reactions induced by light nuclei.
the production and propagation of hadrons, and in particular of kaons, in heavy ion collisions.
the production of K+ and π+ in deuteron and α induced nuclear reactions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the K + yield is proportional to the number of nucleons participating in the collision, which in turn is related to the total number of nucleons.
the enhancement is a consequence of both a larger number of collisions and a larger energy per collision.
the K + enhancement is a direct consequence of the increase of the hadronic collision density with increasing number of incident nucleons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the K + enhancement is due to an increase of the number of hadrons and to the energy increase in the hadronic collisions, which is the main reason for the K + enhancement in the alpha case.
the total K + production in the d + A system increases with increasing number N of projectile nucleons as N 2, while the total π + production increases only as N 1.5.
the enhancement of the total K + production cross section is due to an increase of the K + production per hadronic interaction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the K + enhancement in alpha-induced reactions is larger than the π + enhancement.
the production of strange hadrons is enhanced by the number of nucleon-nucleon collisions.
K + production in light-ion reactions is not only sensitive to the energy density but also to the energy available in the collision.
